response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), b1 AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) AS v FROM orderexecutions), above1 AS (SELECT p.ordersmark, p.avg_remain FROM per_order p, b1 WHERE p.avg_remain > b1.v), b2 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS v FROM above1), above2 AS (SELECT a.avg_remain FROM above1 a, b2 WHERE a.avg_remain > b2.v) SELECT AVG(a.avg_remain) AS avg_of_averages, AVG(a.avg_remain - b1.v) AS avg_excess_over_first, AVG(a.avg_remain - b2.v) AS avg_excess_over_second FROM above2 a, b1, b2

assumptions.assumption: The first benchmark is the plain mean of remaincount over all execution rows, ignoring NULLs. This is not the mean of the per-order averages.
Executions with a NULL ordersmark form a single group, as the request says. Orders whose remaincount values are all NULL have a NULL average and drop out at the first comparison.
Both filters are strict (>). The second benchmark is the mean of the averages of orders that passed the first filter.
